records.gloss: and if in truth and in integrity you have acted with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, rejoice in Abimelech, and may rejoice also he in you.
pieces: if, I say, you have acted faithfully and honorably toward Jerubbaal and his family today, then be happy with Abimelech, and may he be happy with you.

L.19: and if you have acted in truth and in integrity with Jerubbaal and with his house this day, rejoice in Abimelech, and may he also rejoice in you.

R.19: If you have been honest and fair to Jerubbaal and his family today, then enjoy having Abimelech as your king, and may he enjoy you!

decisions.choice: if you have acted in truth: the condition of verse 16 taken up again
decisions.reason: After the interruption of verses 17-18, Jotham repeats his "if" and now gives the outcome. The words of verse 16 return so that the hearer can pick up the thread.

decisions.choice: rejoice in Abimelech: bitter irony
decisions.reason: Jotham has just shown that they did not act in good faith, so the blessing is spoken in scorn. The real outcome follows in verse 20.

decisions.choice: if, I say
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "I say" to show that the sentence begun in verse 16 is resumed.

records.source: וְאִם־אַ֕יִן תֵּ֤צֵא אֵשׁ֙ מֵאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וְתֹאכַ֛ל אֶת־בַּעֲלֵ֥י שְׁכֶ֖ם וְאֶת־בֵּ֣ית מִלּ֑וֹא וְתֵצֵ֨א אֵ֜שׁ מִבַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁכֶם֙ וּמִבֵּ֣ית מִלּ֔וֹא וְתֹאכַ֖ל אֶת־אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And if not, may fire go out from Abimelech and may it consume [the] lords of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire go out from [the] lords of Shechem and from Beth-millo and may it consume Abimelech.
pieces: But if not, may fire come out from Abimelech and burn up the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo, and may fire come out from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and burn up Abimelech!"

L.20: But if not, let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo, and let fire come out from the lords of Shechem and from Beth-millo and devour Abimelech."

R.20: But if you have not, may fire come from Abimelech and burn up the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo! And may fire break out from the leaders of Shechem and Beth-millo and burn up Abimelech!"

decisions.choice: fire from Abimelech: the bramble's fire of verse 15 applied
decisions.reason: Abimelech is the bramble, and the lords of Shechem are the trees that chose him. Each side will destroy the other. The curse comes true when Abimelech burns the Tower of Shechem (verse 49) and is himself killed (verses 53-54); verse 57 calls it "the curse of Jotham".

decisions.choice: a curse laid before God
decisions.reason: Jotham has asked God to listen (verse 7). His words are not a magic spell but an appeal for God to judge between the two sides, and the narrator says that God did so (verses 23-24, 56-57).

records.source: וַיָּ֣נָס יוֹתָ֔ם וַיִּבְרַ֖ח וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ בְּאֵ֑רָה וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב שָׁ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י אֲבִימֶ֥לֶךְ אָחִֽיו׃פ
records.gloss: And fled Jotham and ran away and went to Beer and dwelt there from before Abimelech his brother.
pieces: Then Jotham ran for his life. He escaped to Beer and settled there, out of the reach of his brother Abimelech.

L.21: And Jotham fled and ran away and went to Beer, and he lived there away from Abimelech his brother.

R.21: Then Jotham ran away. He went to the town of Beer and lived there, because he was afraid of his brother Abimelech.

decisions.choice: Beer: a town whose site is unknown
decisions.reason: The name means "well", and several places in Israel bore it (Numbers 21:16). Which one Jotham fled to is not known; it was far enough from Abimelech to be safe.

decisions.choice: from before Abimelech: to escape him, for fear of him
decisions.reason: "From before" someone means out of his presence, often in fear (1 Samuel 21:11). Jotham is safe only where Abimelech cannot reach him.

decisions.choice: because he was afraid of
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly why Jotham stayed away (m2), and adds "the town of" before Beer.

records.source: וַיָּ֧שַׂר אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל שָׁלֹ֥שׁ שָׁנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And ruled Abimelech over Israel three years.
pieces: Abimelech held power over Israel for three years.

L.22: And Abimelech ruled over Israel three years.

R.22: Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.

decisions.choice: ruled: held power, not "reigned as king"
decisions.reason: The verb here is not the one for reigning as king that the chapter has used (verses 6, 8-14), nor "judged" (2:16). It means to act as a prince or commander. The narrator holds back the title the lords of Shechem gave him.

decisions.choice: over Israel: over the part of Israel he controlled
decisions.reason: Abimelech's power seems to reach no further than Shechem and the towns near it (verses 41, 50), but those who fought for him are called "the men of Israel" (verse 55). "Israel" here is the Israelite people he held under him, not necessarily all the tribes.

records.heading: Shechem turns against Abimelech

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח אֱלֹהִים֙ ר֣וּחַ רָעָ֔ה בֵּ֣ין אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וּבֵ֖ין בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּבְגְּד֥וּ בַעֲלֵי־שְׁכֶ֖ם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And sent God a spirit of evil between Abimelech and between [the] lords of Shechem, and dealt treacherously [the] lords of Shechem with Abimelech,
pieces: Then God sent an evil spirit to come between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem broke faith with Abimelech,

L.23: And God sent an evil spirit between Abimelech and the lords of Shechem, and the lords of Shechem dealt treacherously with Abimelech,

R.23: Then God sent an evil spirit that turned Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem against each other. The leaders of Shechem turned traitor against Abimelech.

decisions.choice: an evil spirit: a spirit that brings harm and strife
decisions.reason: The word ra'ah can mean moral evil, but also harm, trouble or disaster (Amos 3:6; Isaiah 45:7). Here the spirit does its work "between" two allies, so it brings ill will and division. The same phrase is used of the spirit that troubled Saul (1 Samuel 16:14-16; 18:10). Whether a spirit-being is meant or a temper of hostility sent among them, the Hebrew does not say.

decisions.choice: God sent it: God acts in judgment through the people's own falseness
decisions.reason: The narrator gives the reason at once (verse 24): the murder of the seventy must be repaid. God does not make the lords sin; they had already acted without good faith (verses 16-19). God turns the alliance they built on murder against itself, as Jotham had asked (verses 7, 20). Scripture speaks the same way of God sending a deceiving spirit to judge King Ahab (1 Kings 22:19-23). God remains the judge who pays back evil (verses 56-57), not its author.

decisions.choice: dealt treacherously: broke faith, betrayed
decisions.reason: The verb is used of breaking a covenant or a marriage (Malachi 2:14; Jeremiah 3:20). The men who chose Abimelech "in truth" (verses 16, 19) now betray him in turn.

decisions.choice: that turned ... against each other
decisions.reason: Readable says what the spirit did "between" them, as the second half of the verse shows (m1).

decisions.choice: broke faith with
decisions.reason: Balanced says "broke faith with" for the verb of betrayal; Literal keeps "dealt treacherously".

records.source: לָב֕וֹא חֲמַ֖ס שִׁבְעִ֣ים בְּנֵֽי־יְרֻבָּ֑עַל וְדָמָ֗ם לָשׂ֞וּם עַל־אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ אֲחִיהֶם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר הָרַ֣ג אוֹתָ֔ם וְעַל֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם אֲשֶׁר־חִזְּק֥וּ אֶת־יָדָ֖יו לַהֲרֹ֥ג אֶת־אֶחָֽיו׃
records.gloss: to come [the] violence [done to the] seventy sons of Jerubbaal, and their blood to put on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on [the] lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.
pieces: so that the violence done to the seventy sons of Jerubbaal would come back on those who did it, and the guilt for their blood would fall on their brother Abimelech, who killed them, and on the leaders of Shechem, who helped him kill his brothers.

L.24: so that the violence [done to] the seventy sons of Jerubbaal might come, and their blood be laid on Abimelech their brother, who killed them, and on the lords of Shechem, who strengthened his hands to kill his brothers.

R.24: God did this so that Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem would be punished for the murder of Jerubbaal's seventy sons. Abimelech had killed his own brothers, and the leaders of Shechem had helped him do it.

decisions.choice: for the violence to come: for the crime to come back on those who did it
decisions.reason: Violence that "comes" is wrong that returns on the doer (Psalm 7:17). The verse names the purpose of what God did in verse 23.

decisions.choice: to put their blood on Abimelech: to make him bear the guilt of their murder
decisions.reason: Shed blood cries out for justice (Genesis 4:10; 9:6), and to have someone's blood "on" you is to carry the guilt for his death (Deuteronomy 19:10; 2 Samuel 1:16).

decisions.choice: who strengthened his hands: who backed him and made the murder possible
decisions.reason: To strengthen someone's hands is to give him the means and the courage to act (1 Samuel 23:16; Jeremiah 23:14). The lords gave Abimelech the silver to hire his men (verse 4).

decisions.choice: God did this
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and names God as the one acting, from verse 23.

decisions.choice: would come back on those who did it
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out what it means for the violence to "come" (m1); Literal keeps the bare verb.

records.source: וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ לוֹ֩ בַעֲלֵ֨י שְׁכֶ֜ם מְאָרְבִ֗ים עַ֚ל רָאשֵׁ֣י הֶהָרִ֔ים וַיִּגְזְל֗וּ אֵ֛ת כָּל־אֲשֶׁר־יַעֲבֹ֥ר עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם בַּדָּ֑רֶךְ וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃פ
records.gloss: And set for him [the] lords of Shechem ambushers on [the] tops of the mountains, and they robbed all who passed by them on the road. And it was told to Abimelech.
pieces: The leaders of Shechem set men in ambush against him on the mountaintops, and they robbed everyone who came past them along the road. Abimelech was told about it.

L.25: And the lords of Shechem set men lying in wait for him on the tops of the mountains, and they robbed everyone who passed by them on the road. And it was told to Abimelech.

R.25: The leaders of Shechem hid men on the hilltops to attack Abimelech. Those men robbed everyone who traveled along the road nearby. Someone told Abimelech what was happening.

decisions.choice: set ambushers for him: to waylay Abimelech, and to his harm
decisions.reason: "For him" can mean against him, lying in wait to catch him on the road, or to his harm, by robbing travelers he was meant to protect. The robbery shows that his rule could not keep the roads safe, and it may have cut off the tolls and trade he lived on.

decisions.choice: robbing travelers on the mountain roads
decisions.reason: Shechem lies in a pass between Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, on a main road through the hill country. Bandits on the heights above it could stop all traffic through the pass.

decisions.choice: to attack Abimelech
decisions.reason: Readable takes "for him" as "against him", the first sense of m1, and keeps the robbery that follows.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֞א גַּ֤עַל בֶּן־עֶ֨בֶד֙ וְאֶחָ֔יו וַיַּעַבְר֖וּ בִּשְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּבְטְחוּ־ב֖וֹ בַּעֲלֵ֥י שְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And came Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers, and they passed over into Shechem, and trusted in him [the] lords of Shechem.
pieces: Then Gaal son of Ebed arrived with his relatives and moved into Shechem, and the leaders of Shechem came to trust him.

L.26: And Gaal son of Ebed came with his brothers, and they moved into Shechem, and the lords of Shechem put their trust in him.

R.26: Then a man named Gaal son of Ebed moved to Shechem with his relatives. The leaders of Shechem began to trust him.

decisions.choice: Gaal son of Ebed: a newcomer to Shechem
decisions.reason: Nothing is said of where Gaal came from. His father's name, Ebed, is the common word for "slave", and the story may enjoy the irony: the man who scorns serving Abimelech (verse 28) is "son of a slave", the charge Jotham made against Abimelech (verse 18).

decisions.choice: passed over into Shechem: came in and settled there
decisions.reason: The verb means to cross over or pass through; here it is the arrival of Gaal's clan in the city, where they stay (verse 41).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 1, "brothers" means kinsmen; Balanced and Readable say "relatives".

records.source: וַיֵּצְא֨וּ הַשָּׂדֶ֜ה וַֽיִּבְצְר֤וּ אֶת־כַּרְמֵיהֶם֙ וַֽיִּדְרְכ֔וּ וַֽיַּעֲשׂ֖וּ הִלּוּלִ֑ים וַיָּבֹ֨אוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אֱֽלֹֽהֵיהֶ֔ם וַיֹּֽאכְלוּ֙ וַיִּשְׁתּ֔וּ וַֽיְקַלְל֖וּ אֶת־אֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And they went out [to] the field and gathered [the grapes of] their vineyards and trod [them] and made festival praises, and went into [the] house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.
pieces: They went out to the fields, harvested the grapes from their vineyards and trod them, and held a harvest festival. They went into the temple of their god, ate and drank, and cursed Abimelech.

L.27: And they went out into the field and gathered [the grapes of] their vineyards and trod [them] and held a festival of praise, and they went into the house of their god and ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

R.27: At harvest time they went out to their vineyards, picked the grapes, and crushed them to make wine. Then they held a festival. They went into the temple of their god, where they ate and drank and cursed Abimelech.

decisions.choice: a festival of praise: the thanksgiving feast at the grape harvest
decisions.reason: The word means praises or rejoicing, and is used of fruit set apart to give thanks at harvest (Leviticus 19:24). When the grapes had been gathered and trodden, the people feasted in the temple.

decisions.choice: the house of their god: the temple of Baal-berith
decisions.reason: Their god is Baal-berith (verse 4; 8:33), also called El-berith (verse 46). The feast that ought to thank God is held in Baal's house, and turns into a feast of cursing.

decisions.choice: temple
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, "house" of a god is its temple.

decisions.choice: At harvest time ... to make wine
decisions.reason: Readable explains what gathering and treading the grapes meant.

records.source: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר׀גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־עֶ֗בֶד מִֽי־אֲבִימֶ֤לֶךְ וּמִֽי־שְׁכֶם֙ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֔נּוּ הֲלֹ֥א בֶן־יְרֻבַּ֖עַל וּזְבֻ֣ל פְּקִיד֑וֹ עִבְד֗וּ אֶת־אַנְשֵׁ֤י חֲמוֹר֙ אֲבִ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם וּמַדּ֖וּעַ נַעַבְדֶ֥נּוּ אֲנָֽחְנוּ׃
records.gloss: And said Gaal son of Ebed, who [is] Abimelech and who [is] Shechem, that we should serve him? [Is he] not [the] son of Jerubbaal, and Zebul his officer? Serve [the] men of Hamor, [the] father of Shechem! And why should we serve him, we?
pieces: Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is Abimelech, and what is Shechem, that we should be his servants? Is he not Jerubbaal's son, with Zebul as his deputy? Serve the men of Hamor, Shechem's father! Why should we serve Abimelech?

L.28: And Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who [is] Abimelech, and who [is] Shechem, that we should serve him? [Is he] not the son of Jerubbaal, and [is not] Zebul his officer? Serve the men of Hamor the father of Shechem! Why should we serve him?

R.28: Gaal son of Ebed said, "Who is this Abimelech? And who are we in Shechem, that we should serve him? He is only Jerubbaal's son, and Zebul is only his deputy! Serve the family of Hamor, the father of Shechem! Why should we serve Abimelech?

decisions.choice: who is Shechem: what is Shechem, that it should serve such a man?
alternatives: who is the son of Shechem
decisions.reason: Gaal sets the city's name beside Abimelech's: Shechem, an old and proud city, should not be the servant of Jerubbaal's son. Others take "Shechem" to point to Abimelech himself, as the man of Shechem by his mother, or read the line with a small change as "who is the son of Shechem". The sense is uncertain.

decisions.choice: serve the men of Hamor: a command in the Hebrew
alternatives: they served the men of Hamor
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "serve!", urging the city to obey the old ruling family of Shechem rather than Abimelech. The Greek translation reads "he served" or "they served", making it a statement: Jerubbaal's house once served Hamor's men. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: Hamor the father of Shechem: the city's first ruling family
decisions.reason: Hamor was the Hivite prince of Shechem in Jacob's day, and his son was named Shechem (Genesis 33:19; 34:2). Gaal stirs up pride in the old native families against Abimelech, whose father was an Israelite from Ophrah.

decisions.choice: Zebul his officer: the governor Abimelech had put over the city
decisions.reason: The word means one appointed or put in charge, a deputy (Genesis 41:34). Verse 30 calls Zebul the ruler of the city.

decisions.choice: who are we in Shechem
decisions.reason: Readable gives the sense chosen in m1, that the city's own standing is meant.

decisions.choice: Abimelech
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Abimelech for "him" at the end, where several men have just been named.

records.source: וּמִ֨י יִתֵּ֜ן אֶת־הָעָ֤ם הַזֶּה֙ בְּיָדִ֔י וְאָסִ֖ירָה אֶת־אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לַאֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ רַבֶּ֥ה צְבָאֲךָ֖ וָצֵֽאָה׃
records.gloss: And who would give this people into my hand! And I would remove Abimelech. And he said to Abimelech, increase your army and come out.
pieces: If only this people were under my command! I would get rid of Abimelech." And he said to Abimelech, "Build up your army and come out and fight!"

L.29: If only this people were in my hand! Then I would remove Abimelech." And he said to Abimelech, "Increase your army and come out."

R.29: If only I were the leader of these people! I would get rid of Abimelech." Then Gaal shouted a challenge to Abimelech: "Gather your army and come out and fight!"

decisions.choice: who would give this people into my hand: if only I had command of them
decisions.reason: "Who will give ...?" is the usual Hebrew way of saying "if only" (Numbers 11:29; 2 Samuel 19:1). "Into my hand" means under my control.

decisions.choice: and he said to Abimelech: Gaal's challenge, spoken against an absent rival
alternatives: and I would say to Abimelech
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has "he said". The Greek translation reads "and I would say", which makes the challenge part of Gaal's boast; the two differ by one letter. Abimelech is not in the city (verse 31), so in the Hebrew the challenge is a taunt for others to carry to him. The Hebrew text is followed.

decisions.choice: increase your army and come out: a dare to come and fight
decisions.reason: "Come out" is the word for marching out to battle (verses 33, 38).

decisions.choice: and fight
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "and fight" to make the challenge clear.

decisions.choice: shouted a challenge
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the words are a challenge thrown out, not a message delivered (m2).

records.source: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע זְבֻל֙ שַׂר־הָעִ֔יר אֶת־דִּבְרֵ֖י גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־עָ֑בֶד וַיִּ֖חַר אַפּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And heard Zebul, [the] ruler of the city, [the] words of Gaal son of Ebed, and burned his anger.
pieces: When Zebul, the governor of the city, heard what Gaal son of Ebed had said, he was furious.

L.30: And Zebul, the ruler of the city, heard the words of Gaal son of Ebed, and his anger burned.

R.30: Zebul, the man in charge of the city, heard what Gaal said, and he became very angry.

decisions.choice: the ruler of the city: the governor who ran Shechem for Abimelech
decisions.reason: The word sar names an official with power over others. "The sar of the city" is its governor (1 Kings 22:26; 2 Kings 23:8). Zebul is Abimelech's deputy (verse 28), loyal to him while Abimelech lives elsewhere (verse 41).

decisions.choice: his anger burned: he became very angry
decisions.reason: Anger is pictured as heat in the face or nostrils, a common Hebrew way of speaking (Genesis 30:2; Exodus 32:19).

decisions.choice: ruler (L), governor (B), the man in charge (R)
decisions.reason: Here sar is the head of a city, not a court official or an army commander, so "prince" and "commander" do not fit. Literal says "ruler", Balanced "governor", Readable "the man in charge".

records.source: וַיִּשְׁלַ֧ח מַלְאָכִ֛ים אֶל־אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בְּתָרְמָ֣ה לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּה֩ גַ֨עַל בֶּן־עֶ֤בֶד וְאֶחָיו֙ בָּאִ֣ים שְׁכֶ֔מָה וְהִנָּ֛ם צָרִ֥ים אֶת־הָעִ֖יר עָלֶֽיךָ׃
records.gloss: And he sent messengers to Abimelech in deceit, saying, look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers [are] coming to Shechem, and look, they [are] stirring up the city against you.
pieces: He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech to say, "Gaal son of Ebed and his relatives have come to Shechem, and they are turning the city against you.

L.31: And he sent messengers to Abimelech in secret, saying, "Look, Gaal son of Ebed and his brothers have come to Shechem, and look, they are stirring up the city against you.

R.31: He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech with this message: "Gaal son of Ebed and his relatives have come to Shechem. They are turning the people of the city against you.

decisions.choice: in deceit: secretly, by stealth
decisions.reason: The word means deceit or trickery: Zebul acts behind Gaal's back while pretending to be on his side (verses 36-38). Some take it as a place name, "at Tormah", perhaps the same as Arumah (verse 41), where Abimelech was staying.

decisions.choice: stirring up the city against you: turning the city to hostility
decisions.reason: The verb usually means to besiege or shut in. Said of a city "against" its ruler, it may mean rousing it to revolt, or shutting its gates against him. Either way Shechem is being closed to Abimelech.

decisions.choice: "look" left out
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable leave out the two "look"s, which mark urgent news in Hebrew; the plain wording and the haste of the message carry it. Literal keeps them.

records.source: וְעַתָּה֙ ק֣וּם לַ֔יְלָה אַתָּ֖ה וְהָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתָּ֑ךְ וֶאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And now, arise by night, you and the people who [are] with you, and lie in wait in the field.
pieces: So now, set out during the night, you and the troops with you, and lie in ambush in the open country.

L.32: And now, rise up by night, you and the people who [are] with you, and lie in wait in the field.

R.32: So come during the night with your men and hide in the fields outside the city.

decisions.choice: the people with you: your fighting men
decisions.reason: "The people" here are Abimelech's troops, as often in battle stories (Exodus 14:6; Joshua 8:1).

decisions.choice: the field: the open country outside the city walls
decisions.reason: "The field" is the land outside a town, its farmland and pasture, where men could hide among the crops and terraces.

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: Balanced says "troops" and Readable "men" for "the people" in the sense of m1; Literal keeps "the people". The same is done through the battle that follows.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה בַבֹּ֨קֶר֙ כִּזְרֹ֣חַ הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ תַּשְׁכִּ֖ים וּפָשַׁטְתָּ֣ עַל־הָעִ֑יר וְהִנֵּה־ה֞וּא וְהָעָ֤ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ֙ יֹצְאִ֣ים אֵלֶ֔יךָ וְעָשִׂ֣יתָ לּ֔וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר תִּמְצָ֥א יָדֶֽךָ׃ס
records.gloss: And it will be in the morning, as the sun rises, you will rise early and rush upon the city; and look, he and the people who [are] with him [are] going out against you, and you will do to him as your hand finds.
pieces: In the morning, as soon as the sun is up, get up early and charge the city. When he and his men come out against you, deal with him however the moment allows."

L.33: And in the morning, as the sun rises, rise early and rush upon the city; and look, [when] he and the people who [are] with him come out against you, you will do to him whatever your hand finds."

R.33: Then early in the morning, at sunrise, attack the city. When Gaal and his men come out to fight you, do whatever you need to do to him."

decisions.choice: do to him as your hand finds: do whatever you have the chance and the power to do
decisions.reason: "As your hand finds" means as opportunity and strength allow (1 Samuel 10:7; 25:8). Zebul leaves the details of the fight to Abimelech.

decisions.choice: rush upon the city: make a sudden attack
decisions.reason: The verb means to spread out or dash, used of raiding parties falling on a place (verse 44; 1 Samuel 23:27).

decisions.choice: Gaal
decisions.reason: Readable names Gaal for "he".

decisions.choice: [when]
decisions.reason: Literal adds "when" in brackets, since the Hebrew "look, he ... going out" pictures what will happen once the attack begins.

records.source: וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְכָל־הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֖וֹ לָ֑יְלָה וַיֶּאֶרְב֣וּ עַל־שְׁכֶ֔ם אַרְבָּעָ֖ה רָאשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And arose Abimelech and all the people who [were] with him by night, and lay in wait against Shechem [in] four companies.
pieces: So Abimelech and all the troops with him set out by night and took up hidden positions around Shechem in four companies.

L.34: And Abimelech and all the people who [were] with him rose up by night and lay in wait against Shechem [in] four companies.

R.34: So Abimelech and all his men came during the night. They split into four groups and hid near Shechem.

decisions.choice: four companies: four units of the army
decisions.reason: The word is "heads", used of the divisions of a fighting force (7:16; 1 Samuel 11:11). Each lay hidden on a different side of the city.

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

records.source: וַיֵּצֵא֙ גַּ֣עַל בֶּן־עֶ֔בֶד וַיַּעֲמֹ֕ד פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וַיָּ֧קָם אֲבִימֶ֛לֶךְ וְהָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּ֖וֹ מִן־הַמַּאְרָֽב׃
records.gloss: And went out Gaal son of Ebed and stood [at the] entrance of [the] gate of the city, and arose Abimelech and the people who [were] with him from the ambush.
pieces: Gaal son of Ebed went out and was standing at the entrance to the city gate when Abimelech and his troops rose up from their hiding places.

L.35: And Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, and Abimelech and the people who [were] with him rose up from the ambush.

R.35: Gaal son of Ebed went out and stood at the city gate. Just then Abimelech and his men came out of their hiding places.

decisions.choice: the entrance of the city gate: the place of public business and of defense
decisions.reason: The gate was where a city's leaders sat to settle its affairs (Ruth 4:1; 2 Samuel 15:2) and where it was defended. Gaal stands there as the man now in charge of Shechem.

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

decisions.choice: Just then
decisions.reason: Readable shows that the two things happen at the same moment, as the Hebrew order implies.

records.source: וַיַּרְא־גַּעַל֮ אֶת־הָעָם֒ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל־זְבֻ֔ל הִנֵּה־עָ֣ם יוֹרֵ֔ד מֵרָאשֵׁ֖י הֶהָרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ זְבֻ֔ל אֵ֣ת צֵ֧ל הֶהָרִ֛ים אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה כָּאֲנָשִֽׁים׃ס
records.gloss: And saw Gaal the people and said to Zebul, look, people coming down from [the] tops of the mountains. And said to him Zebul, [the] shadow of the mountains you [are] seeing as men.
pieces: When Gaal saw the troops, he said to Zebul, "Look, there are people coming down from the mountaintops!" Zebul answered, "You are taking the shadows of the mountains for men."

L.36: And Gaal saw the people and said to Zebul, "Look, people are coming down from the tops of the mountains." And Zebul said to him, "You are seeing the shadow of the mountains as [if they were] men."

R.36: Gaal saw them and said to Zebul, "Look! People are coming down from the tops of the hills!" But Zebul told him, "Those are only the shadows on the hills. They just look like men to you."

decisions.choice: the shadow of the mountains: shapes in the early light that look like men
decisions.reason: It is sunrise (verse 33), when the shadows on the slopes are long. Zebul, secretly on Abimelech's side (verse 31), makes light of what Gaal sees, to give Abimelech's men time to come close.

decisions.choice: Zebul is with Gaal at the gate
decisions.reason: Zebul stays beside Gaal as if he were an ally. His mocking reply in verse 38 shows that he has played for time on purpose.

decisions.choice: only ... They just look like men
decisions.reason: Readable brings out Zebul's dismissive tone.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨סֶף ע֣וֹד גַּעַל֮ לְדַבֵּר֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּה־עָם֙ יֽוֹרְדִ֔ים מֵעִ֖ם טַבּ֣וּר הָאָ֑רֶץ וְרֹאשׁ־אֶחָ֣ד בָּ֔א מִדֶּ֖רֶךְ אֵל֥וֹן מְעוֹנְנִֽים׃
records.gloss: And again yet Gaal spoke and said, look, people coming down from with [the] navel of the land, and one company coming from [the] way of [the] oak of [the] soothsayers.
pieces: Gaal spoke again: "Look, troops are coming down from the center of the land, and another company is coming by the road from the Soothsayers' Oak!"

L.37: And Gaal spoke again and said, "Look, people are coming down from the navel of the land, and one company is coming by the way of the oak of the soothsayers."

R.37: Gaal spoke again: "Look! Men are coming down from the high ground in the middle of the land! And another group is coming along the road from the Fortune-tellers' Oak!"

decisions.choice: the navel of the land: a high point at the center of the land
decisions.reason: The word means navel, and is used of the land as the center of the world (Ezekiel 38:12). Here it is probably a hill near Shechem thought of as the middle of the land, perhaps a shoulder of Mount Gerizim. Its place is not known.

decisions.choice: the oak of the soothsayers: a tree where people sought omens
decisions.reason: Soothsayers read signs to tell the future, a practice the law forbids (Deuteronomy 18:10, 14). The tree was a known landmark near Shechem; it may be the same as the "oak of Moreh", "oak of the teacher", where Abraham camped (Genesis 12:6).

decisions.choice: troops
decisions.reason: Balanced says "troops" for "people" here, since Gaal is now seeing armed men; Readable says "men".

decisions.choice: the Soothsayers' Oak / the Fortune-tellers' Oak
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable write the landmark as a name. Readable says "fortune-tellers", a commoner word for the same people.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלָ֜יו זְבֻ֗ל אַיֵּ֨ה אֵפ֥וֹא פִ֨יךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תֹּאמַ֔ר מִ֥י אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ כִּ֣י נַעַבְדֶ֑נּוּ הֲלֹ֨א זֶ֤ה הָעָם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר מָאַ֣סְתָּה בּ֔וֹ צֵא־נָ֥א עַתָּ֖ה וְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּֽוֹ׃ס
records.gloss: And said to him Zebul, where [is] then your mouth, which you said, who [is] Abimelech that we should serve him? [Is] not this the people that you despised? Go out, please, now and fight against it.
pieces: Then Zebul said to him, "Where is your big talk now, you who said, 'Who is Abimelech, that we should be his servants?' Are these not the men you looked down on? Go out now and fight them!"

L.38: And Zebul said to him, "Where then [is] your mouth, with which you said, 'Who [is] Abimelech, that we should serve him?' [Is] not this the people that you despised? Go out now, please, and fight against them."

R.38: Then Zebul said to him, "Where is all your bragging now? You said, 'Who is Abimelech? Why should we serve him?' These are the men you made fun of! Go out and fight them now!"

decisions.choice: where is your mouth: what has become of your boasting?
decisions.reason: "Mouth" stands for what Gaal said. Zebul quotes Gaal's own words back to him (verse 28) and now drops his pretense.

decisions.choice: despised: rejected with scorn
decisions.reason: The verb means to reject or treat as worthless (1 Samuel 8:7; 15:23). Gaal had scorned Abimelech and his following.

decisions.choice: your big talk
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of "your mouth" (m1); Literal keeps "your mouth", Readable says "your bragging".

records.source: וַיֵּ֣צֵא גַ֔עַל לִפְנֵ֖י בַּעֲלֵ֣י שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בַּאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And went out Gaal before [the] lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.
pieces: So Gaal went out at the head of the leaders of Shechem and fought Abimelech.

L.39: And Gaal went out before the lords of Shechem and fought against Abimelech.

R.39: So Gaal led the leaders of Shechem out of the city and fought against Abimelech.

decisions.choice: before the lords of Shechem: at their head, leading them
alternatives: in the sight of the lords of Shechem
decisions.reason: "Before" can mean in front of them, leading them into battle, or in their sight, while they watched from the city. Leading them fits best, since Gaal has claimed to be their leader (verse 29).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַיִּרְדְּפֵ֣הוּ אֲבִימֶ֔לֶךְ וַיָּ֖נָס מִפָּנָ֑יו וַֽיִּפְּל֛וּ חֲלָלִ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים עַד־פֶּ֥תַח הַשָּֽׁעַר׃
records.gloss: And pursued him Abimelech, and he fled from before him, and fell slain many to [the] entrance of the gate.
pieces: Abimelech chased him, and Gaal ran from him. Many fell dead along the way, right up to the entrance of the gate.

L.40: And Abimelech pursued him, and he fled before him, and many fell slain, up to the entrance of the gate.

R.40: Abimelech chased Gaal, and Gaal ran away from him. Many of Gaal's men were killed on the way back to the city gate.

decisions.choice: slain: struck down, killed or fatally wounded
decisions.reason: The word means pierced, those struck down in battle (Deuteronomy 21:1). The rout reaches the very gate from which Gaal had gone out.

decisions.choice: Gaal
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Gaal where the Hebrew says "he"; Readable also makes clear that the dead were Gaal's men.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ בָּארוּמָ֑ה וַיְגָ֧רֶשׁ זְבֻ֛ל אֶת־גַּ֥עַל וְאֶת־אֶחָ֖יו מִשֶּׁ֥בֶת בִּשְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And stayed Abimelech at Arumah, and drove out Zebul Gaal and his brothers from dwelling in Shechem.
pieces: Abimelech then stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove Gaal and his relatives out, so that they could no longer live in Shechem.

L.41: And Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul drove out Gaal and his brothers from living in Shechem.

R.41: Abimelech stayed in the town of Arumah. Zebul forced Gaal and his relatives to leave Shechem.

decisions.choice: Arumah: a town near Shechem, perhaps Abimelech's base
decisions.reason: Arumah is not named anywhere else; it was probably a few miles from Shechem. Abimelech does not live in Shechem itself but rules it through Zebul (verses 28, 30).

decisions.choice: relatives
decisions.reason: As in verse 26.

records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ מִֽמָּחֳרָ֔ת וַיֵּצֵ֥א הָעָ֖ם הַשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּגִּ֖דוּ לַאֲבִימֶֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And it was on the next day, and went out the people [to] the field, and they told Abimelech.
pieces: On the following day the people of Shechem came out to the fields, and someone reported it to Abimelech.

L.42: And it happened on the next day that the people went out into the field, and they told Abimelech.

R.42: The next day the people of Shechem went out to work in their fields. Someone told Abimelech about it.

decisions.choice: the people: the people of Shechem, not Abimelech's troops
decisions.reason: Here "the people" are the townspeople, who go out into the fields once Gaal has gone, perhaps thinking the danger is over. Abimelech treats it as a chance to strike.

decisions.choice: of Shechem
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose people are meant (m1).

decisions.choice: to work in
decisions.reason: Readable says why they went to the fields. The Hebrew does not say; work on the land is the likeliest reason, but they may have gone out armed.

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֣ח אֶת־הָעָ֗ם וַֽיֶּחֱצֵם֙ לִשְׁלֹשָׁ֣ה רָאשִׁ֔ים וַיֶּאֱרֹ֖ב בַּשָּׂדֶ֑ה וַיַּ֗רְא וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָעָם֙ יֹצֵ֣א מִן־הָעִ֔יר וַיָּ֥קָם עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם וַיַּכֵּֽם׃
records.gloss: And he took the people and divided them into three companies and lay in wait in the field; and he looked, and look, the people coming out from the city, and he rose against them and struck them.
pieces: He took his troops, split them into three companies, and set an ambush in the fields. As soon as he saw people leaving the city, he rose and attacked them.

L.43: And he took the people and divided them into three companies and lay in wait in the field. And he looked, and look, the people were coming out from the city, and he rose up against them and struck them.

R.43: Abimelech divided his army into three groups, and they hid in the fields. As soon as he saw people leaving the city, he jumped up and attacked them.

decisions.choice: the people ... the people: first his troops, then the townspeople
decisions.reason: The same word is used twice in one verse with two meanings: the army Abimelech leads, and the people of Shechem coming out of the city (verse 42).

decisions.choice: troops / army
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

records.source: וַאֲבִימֶ֗לֶךְ וְהָרָאשִׁים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עִמּ֔וֹ פָּשְׁט֕וּ וַיַּ֣עַמְד֔וּ פֶּ֖תַח שַׁ֣עַר הָעִ֑יר וּשְׁנֵ֣י הָֽרָאשִׁ֗ים פָּֽשְׁט֛וּ עַֽל־כָּל־אֲשֶׁ֥ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֖ה וַיַּכּֽוּם׃
records.gloss: And Abimelech and the companies who [were] with him rushed and stood [at the] entrance of [the] gate of the city, and the two companies rushed upon all who [were] in the field and struck them.
pieces: Abimelech and the forces with him charged forward and took their stand at the entrance to the city gate, while the other two companies charged at everyone in the fields and struck them down.

L.44: And Abimelech and the companies that [were] with him rushed forward and stood at the entrance of the gate of the city, and the two [other] companies rushed upon all who [were] in the field and struck them.

R.44: Abimelech and the men with him rushed forward and took their place at the city gate, so that no one could get back in. The other two groups attacked the people in the fields and killed them.

decisions.choice: the companies with him: one company with Abimelech, two in the fields
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the plural "companies", but verse 43 gives three companies and this verse sends "the two" against the fields, so only one can have been with Abimelech. Some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations have the singular "company". The plural may be a copying slip or a loose way of speaking; the sense is clear either way.

decisions.choice: standing at the gate: cutting off the way back into the city
decisions.reason: By holding the gate, Abimelech kept the people in the fields from escaping into Shechem while his other companies attacked them.

decisions.choice: the forces / the men with him
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable do not repeat the plural "companies" here, which would make four companies in all; they say "forces" and "men" (m1). Literal keeps "companies".

decisions.choice: so that no one could get back in
decisions.reason: Readable says why Abimelech held the gate (m2).

records.source: וַאֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ נִלְחָ֣ם בָּעִ֗יר כֹּ֚ל הַיּ֣וֹם הַה֔וּא וַיִּלְכֹּד֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וְאֶת־הָעָ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־בָּ֖הּ הָרָ֑ג וַיִּתֹּץ֙ אֶת־הָעִ֔יר וַיִּזְרָעֶ֖הָ מֶֽלַח׃פ
records.gloss: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and captured the city, and the people who [were] in it he killed, and he tore down the city and sowed it [with] salt.
pieces: Abimelech fought against the city all that day. He captured it and killed the people in it; then he tore the city down and scattered salt over it.

L.45: And Abimelech fought against the city all that day, and he captured the city and killed the people who [were] in it, and he tore down the city and sowed it [with] salt.

R.45: Abimelech fought against Shechem all day long. He captured the city and killed the people who were in it. Then he destroyed the city and spread salt over the ground.

decisions.choice: sowed it with salt: marked it for lasting ruin
decisions.reason: Salt makes soil barren, and land "burned with salt" is a picture of ruin under a curse (Deuteronomy 29:22; Jeremiah 17:6). Scattering salt over the city was a sign that it should lie waste. The man who was made king in Shechem destroys it.

decisions.choice: he tore down the city: the town itself, while its tower still stood
decisions.reason: The Tower of Shechem is still held after this (verses 46-49), so the city's houses and walls are meant. Shechem was rebuilt long afterward (1 Kings 12:25).

decisions.choice: Shechem
decisions.reason: Readable names the city.

records.source: וַֽיִּשְׁמְע֔וּ כָּֽל־בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל־שְׁכֶ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ אֶל־צְרִ֔יחַ בֵּ֖ית אֵ֥ל בְּרִֽית׃
records.gloss: And heard all [the] lords of [the] Tower of Shechem, and they went into [the] stronghold of [the] house of El-berith.
pieces: When all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem heard this, they went into the stronghold of the temple of El-berith.

L.46: And all the lords of the Tower of Shechem heard, and they went into the stronghold of the house of El-berith.

R.46: All the leaders of the Tower of Shechem heard what had happened. So they went into the strong inner room of the temple of the god El-berith.

decisions.choice: the Tower of Shechem: the fortified quarter of the city, near the temple
decisions.reason: The tower was a strong building or quarter of its own, apart from the town that Abimelech had taken. It may be the same as Beth-millo (verses 6, 20).

decisions.choice: the stronghold: an inner chamber or vault of the temple
decisions.reason: The word is rare (1 Samuel 13:6 uses it of hiding places in the hills) and its exact sense is uncertain. It seems to be a fortified inner room or cellar in the temple, where people could shut themselves in.

decisions.choice: El-berith: "God of the covenant", the god of verse 4
decisions.reason: El-berith is another name for Baal-berith, "Baal of the covenant" (verse 4; 8:33). The lords who took his silver to pay for murder now look to his house for safety.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

decisions.choice: the strong inner room ... the god
decisions.reason: Readable explains "stronghold" (m2) and adds "the god" as in verse 4.

records.source: וַיֻּגַּ֖ד לַאֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ כִּ֣י הִֽתְקַבְּצ֔וּ כָּֽל־בַּעֲלֵ֖י מִֽגְדַּל־שְׁכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And it was told to Abimelech that had gathered themselves all [the] lords of [the] Tower of Shechem.
pieces: Abimelech was told that all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem had gathered there.

L.47: And it was told to Abimelech that all the lords of the Tower of Shechem had gathered together.

R.47: Someone told Abimelech that all the leaders of the Tower of Shechem were gathered in one place.

decisions.choice: had gathered together: all in one place
decisions.reason: The point of the report is that they are all in one place, which makes the trap that follows possible.

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַיַּ֨עַל אֲבִימֶ֜לֶךְ הַר־צַלְמ֗וֹן הוּא֮ וְכָל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־אִתּוֹ֒ וַיִּקַּח֩ אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ אֶת־הַקַּרְדֻּמּ֜וֹת בְּיָד֗וֹ וַיִּכְרֹת֙ שׂוֹכַ֣ת עֵצִ֔ים וַיִּ֨שָּׂאֶ֔הָ וַיָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־שִׁכְמ֑וֹ וַיֹּ֜אמֶר אֶל־הָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־עִמּ֗וֹ מָ֤ה רְאִיתֶם֙ עָשִׂ֔יתִי מַהֲר֖וּ עֲשׂ֥וּ כָמֽוֹנִי׃
records.gloss: And went up Abimelech [to] Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who [were] with him, and took Abimelech the axes in his hand and cut a branch of trees and lifted it and put [it] on his shoulder, and said to the people who [were] with him, what you have seen I have done, hurry, do like me.
pieces: Abimelech and all his troops went up Mount Zalmon. He took an axe in his hand, cut a branch from the trees, lifted it up and put it on his shoulder. Then he said to the men with him, "Quick! Do just what you have seen me do!"

L.48: And Abimelech went up Mount Zalmon, he and all the people who [were] with him, and Abimelech took the axe in his hand and cut off a branch of the trees, and he lifted it and put [it] on his shoulder, and he said to the people who [were] with him, "What you have seen me do, hurry, do as I [have done]."

R.48: Abimelech and all his men climbed Mount Zalmon. There he took an axe and cut off a branch from a tree. He lifted it onto his shoulder and told his men, "Hurry! Do what you saw me do!"

decisions.choice: Mount Zalmon: a wooded hill near Shechem
decisions.reason: The name may mean "dark" or "shady", fitting a wooded hill. It is not certain which hill it was; Mount Ebal, across the valley from Gerizim, is one suggestion.

decisions.choice: the axes in his hand: an axe, the plural form used for one tool
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has the plural with "in his hand", so it is best taken as one axe (the word is plural also in 1 Samuel 13:21 and Psalm 74:5). Some think he took axes for his men as well.

decisions.choice: cutting branches from the trees: the bramble's fire of the fable
decisions.reason: In Jotham's fable the trees choose the bramble, and fire from the bramble burns them (verse 15). Now Abimelech cuts wood from the trees to burn those who made him king (verse 20).

decisions.choice: troops / men
decisions.reason: As in verse 32, "the people" with Abimelech are his fighting men: "troops" at Balanced, "men" at Readable.

decisions.choice: the axe
decisions.reason: Literal says "the axe" with the sense of m2, since "the axes in his hand" would mislead.

records.source: וַיִּכְרְת֨וּ גַם־כָּל־הָעָ֜ם אִ֣ישׁ שׂוֹכֹ֗ה וַיֵּ֨לְכ֜וּ אַחֲרֵ֤י אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ וַיָּשִׂ֣ימוּ עַֽל־הַצְּרִ֔יחַ וַיַּצִּ֧יתוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֛ם אֶֽת־הַצְּרִ֖יחַ בָּאֵ֑שׁ וַיָּמֻ֜תוּ גַּ֣ם כָּל־אַנְשֵׁ֧י מִֽגְדַּל־שְׁכֶ֛ם כְּאֶ֖לֶף אִ֥ישׁ וְאִשָּֽׁה׃פ
records.gloss: And cut also all the people, each his branch, and went after Abimelech and put [them] on the stronghold and set on fire over them the stronghold with fire, and died also all [the] men of [the] Tower of Shechem, about a thousand, man and woman.
pieces: So all the troops also cut down a branch each and followed Abimelech. They piled the branches against the stronghold and set it on fire over the people inside. So all the {{gender:people|men}} of the Tower of Shechem died too, about 1,000 men and women.

L.49: And all the people also cut down each one his branch and followed Abimelech, and they put [them] against the stronghold and set the stronghold on fire over them, and so all the {{gender:people|men}} of the Tower of Shechem also died, about 1,000 men and women.

R.49: So each of his men cut a branch and followed Abimelech. They piled the branches against the inner room and set it on fire with the people still inside. Everyone in the Tower of Shechem died, about 1,000 men and women.

decisions.choice: set it on fire: Jotham's curse comes true for the lords of Shechem
decisions.reason: Jotham had said, "let fire come out from Abimelech and devour the lords of Shechem and Beth-millo" (verse 20). That fire now burns them in the house of the god whose silver hired Abimelech (verse 4).

decisions.choice: all the men of the Tower: all its people, men and women
decisions.reason: The word usually means men, but the verse itself says the dead were "man and woman", so the whole population of the tower is meant. "About a thousand" is an ordinary round count.

decisions.choice: people (men)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced use the gender setting because the verse counts women among them (m2); the traditional "men" is the alternative. Readable says "everyone".

decisions.choice: the inner room
decisions.reason: Readable says "inner room" for "stronghold", as in verse 46.

records.source: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אֲבִימֶ֖לֶךְ אֶל־תֵּבֵ֑ץ וַיִּ֥חַן בְּתֵבֵ֖ץ וַֽיִּלְכְּדָֽהּ׃
records.gloss: And went Abimelech to Thebez and camped against Thebez and captured it.
pieces: Next Abimelech went to Thebez, laid siege to it, and captured it.

L.50: And Abimelech went to Thebez and camped against Thebez and captured it.

R.50: Then Abimelech went to the town of Thebez. He surrounded it with his army and captured it.

decisions.choice: Thebez: a town north of Shechem
decisions.reason: Thebez is probably the town of Tubas, about ten miles northeast of Shechem. The text does not say why Abimelech attacked it; most likely it too had joined the revolt.

decisions.choice: camped against: laid siege to
decisions.reason: To camp "at" or "against" a town in war means to besiege it (Joshua 10:31).

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" before Thebez.

records.heading: Abimelech dies at Thebez

records.source: וּמִגְדַּל־עֹז֮ הָיָ֣ה בְתוֹךְ־הָעִיר֒ וַיָּנֻ֨סוּ שָׁ֜מָּה כָּל־הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים וְהַנָּשִׁ֗ים וְכֹל֙ בַּעֲלֵ֣י הָעִ֔יר וַֽיִּסְגְּר֖וּ בַּעֲדָ֑ם וַֽיַּעֲל֖וּ עַל־גַּ֥ג הַמִּגְדָּֽל׃
records.gloss: And a tower of strength was in [the] middle of the city, and fled there all the men and the women and all [the] lords of the city, and they shut [the door] behind them, and went up on [the] roof of the tower.
pieces: But inside the city stood a strong tower, and all the men and women and all the leaders of the city fled into it. They shut themselves in and climbed up onto the roof of the tower.

L.51: But a strong tower was in the middle of the city, and all the men and the women and all the lords of the city fled there, and they shut [the door] behind them and went up onto the roof of the tower.

R.51: But inside the city there was a strong tower. All the men and women, with all the leaders of the city, ran into it. They locked the door behind them and climbed up to the roof.

decisions.choice: a strong tower with a flat roof: the town's last refuge
decisions.reason: Many towns had a citadel tower inside the walls where the people could hold out when the walls fell. Its flat roof let the defenders throw down stones and other missiles on attackers below (verse 53).

decisions.choice: leaders
decisions.reason: As in verse 2.

records.source: וַיָּבֹ֤א אֲבִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ עַד־הַמִּגְדָּ֔ל וַיִּלָּ֖חֶם בּ֑וֹ וַיִּגַּ֛שׁ עַד־פֶּ֥תַח הַמִּגְדָּ֖ל לְשָׂרְפ֥וֹ בָאֵֽשׁ׃
records.gloss: And came Abimelech to the tower and fought against it, and drew near to [the] entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.
pieces: Abimelech came up to the tower and attacked it. He went right up to the entrance of the tower to set it on fire.

L.52: And Abimelech came to the tower and fought against it, and he drew near to the entrance of the tower to burn it with fire.

R.52: Abimelech came to the tower and attacked it. He went up close to the door to set the tower on fire.

decisions.choice: to burn it with fire: the same plan as at Shechem
decisions.reason: Abimelech tries again the method that destroyed the Tower of Shechem (verse 49). This time it brings him within reach of the defenders on the roof.

records.source: וַתַּשְׁלֵ֞ךְ אִשָּׁ֥ה אַחַ֛ת פֶּ֥לַח רֶ֖כֶב עַל־רֹ֣אשׁ אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַתָּ֖רִץ אֶת־גֻּלְגָּלְתּֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And threw a woman, one, an upper millstone on [the] head of Abimelech and crushed his skull.
pieces: But a woman dropped an upper millstone on Abimelech's head and cracked his skull.

L.53: And a certain woman threw an upper millstone on the head of Abimelech and crushed his skull.

R.53: Then a woman on the roof dropped a heavy grinding stone on Abimelech's head. It broke his skull.

decisions.choice: an upper millstone: the round stone of a hand mill
decisions.reason: Grain was ground at home between two stones; the upper one, which was moved by hand, could be carried. Grinding was women's daily work (Exodus 11:5). A woman uses an everyday tool to kill the warrior.

decisions.choice: a stone on the head of Abimelech: the end matches the crime
decisions.reason: Abimelech killed his brothers "on one stone" (verses 5, 18), and he dies by a stone. The story of his death was still told in David's day (2 Samuel 11:21).

decisions.choice: on the roof / heavy grinding stone
decisions.reason: Readable says where the woman was (verse 51) and explains "millstone".

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א מְהֵרָ֜ה אֶל־הַנַּ֣עַר׀נֹשֵׂ֣א כֵלָ֗יו וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לוֹ֙ שְׁלֹ֤ף חַרְבְּךָ֙ וּמ֣וֹתְתֵ֔נִי פֶּן־יֹ֥אמְרוּ לִ֖י אִשָּׁ֣ה הֲרָגָ֑תְהוּ וַיִּדְקְרֵ֥הוּ נַעֲר֖וֹ וַיָּמֹֽת׃
records.gloss: And he called quickly to the young man carrying his weapons and said to him, draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, a woman killed him. And pierced him his young man, and he died.
pieces: He quickly called to the young man who carried his armor and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, so that no one can say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" So his young man ran him through, and he died.

L.54: And he called quickly to the young man who carried his weapons and said to him, "Draw your sword and kill me, lest they say of me, 'A woman killed him.'" And his young man pierced him through, and he died.

R.54: Abimelech quickly called to the young man who carried his weapons. He said, "Take out your sword and kill me. I do not want people to say that a woman killed me." So the young man stabbed him, and Abimelech died.

decisions.choice: the young man carrying his weapons: his armor-bearer
decisions.reason: A warrior's attendant carried his shield and spare weapons and fought beside him (1 Samuel 14:1; 31:4).

decisions.choice: lest they say a woman killed him: to die at a woman's hand was a disgrace for a warrior
decisions.reason: Deborah told Barak that the honor of victory would go to a woman (4:9), and Jael killed Sisera (4:21). Abimelech tries to escape that shame, but the story remembers that a woman killed him (2 Samuel 11:21).

decisions.choice: people to say that a woman killed me
decisions.reason: Readable gives the words people might say as indirect speech, to avoid a quotation inside a quotation.

records.source: וַיִּרְא֥וּ אִֽישׁ־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לִמְקֹמֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And saw [the] men of Israel that dead [was] Abimelech, and they went each to his place.
pieces: When the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went back home.

L.55: And the men of Israel saw that Abimelech was dead, and they went each one to his place.

R.55: When the Israelite soldiers saw that Abimelech was dead, they all went back home.

decisions.choice: the men of Israel: the Israelite fighting men who followed Abimelech
decisions.reason: The phrase is used of Israel's army (7:23; 20:11). With their leader dead, the army breaks up and each man goes home.

decisions.choice: each to his place: they went home
decisions.reason: "To go to one's place" means to go home when a campaign or gathering ends (Numbers 24:25).

decisions.choice: soldiers
decisions.reason: Readable says "soldiers" for "men" in the sense of m1.

records.source: וַיָּ֣שֶׁב אֱלֹהִ֔ים אֵ֖ת רָעַ֣ת אֲבִימֶ֑לֶךְ אֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשָׂה֙ לְאָבִ֔יו לַהֲרֹ֖ג אֶת־שִׁבְעִ֥ים אֶחָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And returned God [the] evil of Abimelech that he did to his father by killing his seventy brothers.
pieces: In this way God paid Abimelech back for the evil he had done to his father by murdering his seventy brothers.

L.56: And God returned the evil of Abimelech, which he had done to his father by killing his seventy brothers.

R.56: This is how God punished Abimelech for the evil thing he did to his father when he killed his seventy brothers.

decisions.choice: God returned the evil: God made Abimelech's wrong come back on him
decisions.reason: The narrator names God as the judge behind the events of the chapter: the evil spirit he sent (verse 23), the revolt, the fire and the millstone. The word for "evil" is the one used of that spirit; the harm God sent answers the evil Abimelech had done. Wrongdoing that comes back on the doer is a theme of Israel's wisdom (Psalm 7:17; Proverbs 26:27).

decisions.choice: to his father: a crime against Jerubbaal himself
decisions.reason: Killing a man's sons wiped out his house and his name. Abimelech's crime was against the father as well as the brothers, which is why Jotham asked whether Shechem had dealt fairly with Jerubbaal (verse 16).

decisions.choice: In this way / This is how
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable link the verse to the story just told, as the Hebrew summary implies.

records.source: וְאֵ֗ת כָּל־רָעַת֙ אַנְשֵׁ֣י שְׁכֶ֔ם הֵשִׁ֥יב אֱלֹהִ֖ים בְּרֹאשָׁ֑ם וַתָּבֹ֣א אֲלֵיהֶ֔ם קִֽלֲלַ֖ת יוֹתָ֥ם בֶּן־יְרֻבָּֽעַל׃פ
records.gloss: And all [the] evil of [the] men of Shechem God returned on their head, and came to them [the] curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal.
pieces: God also brought all the evil of the men of Shechem back on their own heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

L.57: And all the evil of the men of Shechem God returned on their heads, and the curse of Jotham son of Jerubbaal came upon them.

R.57: God also punished the men of Shechem for all the evil they had done. What Jotham son of Jerubbaal said in his curse came true for them.

decisions.choice: returned on their head: made their wrong fall on themselves
decisions.reason: To bring something "on someone's head" is to make him bear the consequences of what he has done (1 Kings 2:32-33; Psalm 7:17).

decisions.choice: the curse of Jotham: his words in verse 20 fulfilled
decisions.reason: Jotham had called down fire on both Abimelech and the lords of Shechem (verse 20). Both have now been destroyed, each by the other, as he said.

decisions.choice: God brought it about: the curse came true because God judged
decisions.reason: The verse sets God's repaying and Jotham's curse side by side. The curse had power not of itself but because God, whom Jotham asked to listen (verse 7), judged the wrong done to Jerubbaal's house.

decisions.choice: punished
decisions.reason: Readable says "punished" for the picture of returning evil on their heads (m1).
